motors.notes: The POLOLU-2367's motor and gearbox with a Hall quadrature encoder on the motor shaft: 12 counts per motor revolution (both edges of both channels), 1204.4 per wheel revolution at 100.37:1. Motor power and the encoder share one 6-pin JST SH plug (cable sold separately); the encoder housing reaches past the gearbox on three sides.

batteries.notes: 2S for a Raspberry Pi 5 robot: feeds the bought 5 V regulator (regulators list). The catalog's 6 V Pololu micro-metal gearmotors would see 8.4 V on a full pack, 1.4x rated, over the mech-voltage check's 1.3x limit (7.8 V): a 2S robot needs a motor duty limit (PWM cap near 6/8.4 = 71 %) or 12 V motors.

fullV.where: derived: 2 cells x 4.2 V; guide 'How to maintain the Lipo battery? > Charging': 'Never overcharge batteries over their rated maximal voltage (4.2V/cell for LiPo)'

cutoffV.where: derived: 2 cells x 3.0 V; guide 'How to maintain the Lipo battery? > Discharging': 'Never discharge battery to a level below 3V per cell under load'

maxContA.where: derived: 20 C x 2.2 Ah (spec list 'C-rate: 20C'; the page's usage text says 30C, the lower figure is used), by the guide's formula 'Max continous Amp draw (A)= Battery capacity (Ah) x Discharge rate (C)' (https://gensace.de/pages/lipo-battery-guide)

peakA.where: no burst rating on the page: the 20 C continuous rating is used as the limit (conservative)

regulators.notes: Bought module: powers a Raspberry Pi 5 from a 2S pack with no board circuit. Output is 5 V +/-4 % (the Pi 5's own supply is 5.1 V); the minimum input rises above 5.5 V with load (dropout), so near a 2S pack's 6.0 V cutoff the 5 V rail may sag at full current.

safety.mpn: OMRON A22E-M-01 emergency stop 40 mm red, 1 NC
safety.notes: Its NC contact sits in the motor supply (VBAT to the driver's VM, through the board's e-stop connector): pressing it opens the motors' supply at once, the controller stays on (Eurobot F.4.c tolerates that). Motor current keeps the contact above its 10 mA minimum load; a logic-level sense line (0.3 mA) would sit under it.
